newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral says to continue economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral says to continue economic reforms.

text.p: India's new prime minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, said on Monday that he would press ahead with open-market economic reforms pursued by the two previous governments.
Gujral told reporters after taking the oath of office that he would keep the foreign and finance ministry portfolios for himself in his new centre-left government.
"We will continue the economic reforms and strengthen them," Gujral said.

Gujral retained the entire council of ministers of outgoing prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, except former finance minister P. Chidambaram and labour minister M. Arunachalam were not inducted. Gujral said the other ministers would retain their same portfolios.
Asked to comment on relations with Pakistan, Gujral, who was foreign minister in Deve Gowda's cabinet, said: "Our foreign policy will continue to be the same."

The new prime minister said he would announce his government's plans for the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament, scheduled to reconvene later on Monday. Parliament had been scheduled to take up the budget this week, but the formation of the new government threw the schedule into doubt.
